transcript: 00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out time. quick intro, im maya from redwood inference and with me are ethan and samir. 00:15 Lina (Orchid CTO): hi maya, thanks. lina here, excited to see how this can replace some of our latency spikes. 00:30 Ethan (Redwood SE): cool, i'll start with a brief live sandbox demo, then we'll talk streaming behaviors and retries. note, audio might clip since im switching screens. 00:45 Tara (PM): perfect, we're mostly interested in chat for triage and patient Q&A so low latency is pretty important. 01:10 Ethan (Redwood SE): ok jumping in — this is the hosted API quickstart. you can see the sample request, we default to streaming responses for chat so you can render tokens as they arrive. example here uses curl and websocket clients, but the SDKs do streaming nicely too. 02:05 Rajiv (Lead ML): quick q: how does the KV cache work with chat sessions — can we reuse cached prefixes across short-lived sessions? 02:22 Samir (Optimize): good question, short answer: prefix caching is supported for repeated system prompts and can be shared per-tenant if you pin model variants. it's not a global cross-tenant cache. 02:40 Rajiv (Lead ML): ok makes sense — does caching affect billing? 02:50 Ethan (Redwood SE): billing is token-based, but caching reduces active compute so effectively lowers cost per token; you'll still be billed for returned tokens but compute usage per request drops. 03:20 Lina (Orchid CTO): security: we need SOC2 and SSO SAML for enterprise. do you have docs? 03:30 Samir (Optimize): yes we do — i'll attach the SOC2 pack and our VPC/on-prem checklist. we also support customer-managed K M S for key rotation. 03:55 Noah (SRE): how does private deployment compare to hosted in terms of latency? 04:05 Ethan (Redwood SE): hosted generally gives fastest time-to-value and predictable p99s for small-mid workloads; dedicated pools or private VPCs get you isolated capacity and can reduce tail latency further depending on infra. 04:35 Maya (Redwood AE): important to note we can route by policy — latency-first routing to regional pools and fallback to cheaper model variants if capacity constrained. 05:10 Tara (PM): demo time — show us streaming failure modes and retries. we had problems with partial payloads and duplicate messages in our current system. 05:28 Ethan (Redwood SE): absolutely. i'll simulate a socket interruption and show the recommended client retry logic. watch the timeline: when the stream disconnects, the SDK surfaces a resumable token and then you can re-request with the last acked position. if not resumable, we suggest a restart with idempotency keys to avoid duplicate events. 06:45 Rajiv (Lead ML): are there built-in idempotency primitives? 06:55 Ethan (Redwood SE): yes — request_id headers and idempotency tokens, plus server-side dedupe for short windows. our SDKs wire these for you out of the box. 07:20 Lina (Orchid CTO): what's your recommended backoff strategy? linear or exponential? 07:28 Samir (Optimize): exponential with jitter is our go-to, with server suggested Retry-After headers respected. for streaming we recommend short immediate retries (100-300ms, jittered) then exponential escalation; avoid hammering by using client-side circuit breakers. 08:05 Maya (Redwood AE): also important: model fallbacks — if a high-cost variant is saturated, policy can route to a quantized variant automatically. that helps keep application availability while degrading slightly on quality. 08:35 Rajiv (Lead ML): curious about quantization — does Redwood support INT8 and other quant profiles? 08:45 Ethan (Redwood SE): yes, the runtime supports multiple quant profiles and we surface recommended profiles in the Console Optimize tab based on your workload; we can demo that too. 09:10 Tara (PM): show the console — particularly how we tune parameters like temperature, max tokens, and streaming chunk size. 09:26 Ethan (Redwood SE): sure — console here, route config for the hosted tenant, you can toggle streaming chunk granularity which controls how often partial payloads flush. smaller chunks lower perceived latency but increase token overhead. 10:02 Noah (SRE): are there metrics we can export to prometheus? 10:10 Samir (Optimize): yes, tracing hooks, per-route latency, token counts; we support exporting to prometheus and we also have token-level billing breakdowns in the UI. 10:40 Lina (Orchid CTO): what about failing over regions? we need DR across us-east and eu-west. 10:50 Ethan (Redwood SE): smart routing supports region-aware fallback; you can set a primary region with automatic fallback to secondary if p99 or capacity thresholds hit. note that model state like KV cache isn't replicated cross-region by default — you can enable cross-region cache replication for critical workflows. 11:25 Rajiv (Lead ML): ok that replication sounds heavy, does it impact latency? 11:32 Ethan (Redwood SE): replication is async — it's best for eventual consistency scenarios. for strict low-latency you keep a regional copy and accept a warm-up period. 12:00 Tara (PM): about retries again — we saw double-charges in another vendor when clients retried without idempotency. how do you avoid billing duplication? 12:15 Samir (Optimize): billing uses final output tokens; intermediate retries that don't complete aren't charged beyond compute used. idempotency tokens let us reconcile and avoid duplicate final outputs; we'll show logs where request_ids map to outputs. 13:00 Lina (Orchid CTO): curious on observability — can I replay traces for evaluation? 13:10 Ethan (Redwood SE): yes, console has a trace replay feature for failed requests and you can attach the exact prompt set to the eval harness. 13:40 Rajiv (Lead ML): performance testing — how should we shape test loads? 13:48 Ethan (Redwood SE): provide us a sample RPS profile and sequence length distribution; we'll run a perf harness against hosted pools to produce p50/p95/p99 and cost per token estimates. aim to include peak and steady-state windows. 14:20 Maya (Redwood AE): quick qualification: what's your timeline and success criteria? 14:30 Lina (Orchid CTO): timeline is 6-8 weeks to pilot, success = p95 < 220ms for short queries and predictable cost within 20% of our estimates. 15:05 Rajiv (Lead ML): and data residency — some PHI will remain, we need encryption at rest and in transit and K M S control. 15:15 Samir (Optimize): we support customer K M S, H S M options, and network controls (V P C peering) for private deployments. i'll include the checklist. 15:50 Tara (PM): can you show a quick example of client retry pseudo-code? 16:00 Ethan (Redwood SE): sure — here's a pseudocode snippet: attempt stream, on disconnect check resume token, if present resume, else retry with idempotency key and exponential backoff with jitter; also implement circuit breaker that trips after n failures in short interval. 16:50 Rajiv (Lead ML): what about streaming partial responses causing our front end to display stale suggestions? 17:00 Ethan (Redwood SE): recommend sequence numbers with tokens; only render messages once you receive final chunk marker or adopt optimistic rendering with clear edits when more tokens arrive. 17:30 Lina (Orchid CTO): any limits on connections per tenant? 17:40 Maya (Redwood AE): default limits exist but for pilot we'd provision more concurrent streams. dedicated capacity options then let you set guaranteed concurrency. 18:05 Noah (SRE): firewall and egress rules for sandbox — we need IP allowlist. 18:15 Ethan (Redwood SE): sandbox supports IP allowlist and VPN peering; for production VPC peering or private endpoint is recommended. 18:48 Tara (PM): can Optimize recommend batching windows? sometimes batching increases throughput but hurts latency. 19:00 Samir (Optimize): Optimize surfaces batching sweet spots based on your latency SLOs; for interactive chat it recommends small batch sizes and aggressive prefix caching rather than large batching. 19:35 Rajiv (Lead ML): during the perf run can you include quantized model variants to compare cost/latency tradeoffs? 19:45 Ethan (Redwood SE): yes we can spin the same model in float16 and int8-like quant profiles and show tradeoffs. 20:10 Lina (Orchid CTO): concerns on hallucination control — can you wire evals? 20:20 Samir (Optimize): we have prompt-set tied regression alerts and can run periodic evals; we'll attach the eval harness sample. 20:48 Maya (Redwood AE): quick recap before we wrap: we will give sandbox access, SE will run perf tests, optimize/sr team to share security docs, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff. 21:10 Tara (PM): good — one more ask: sample cost projection for 100k chats/month. 21:20 Maya (Redwood AE): we'll send rough cost model in the pricing packet — depends on tokens per chat and caching hit rate. 21:45 Rajiv (Lead ML): any final gotchas we should know about when moving from our current infra? 21:55 Ethan (Redwood SE): common ones: not tuning chunk size, missing idempotency keys, and not pinning model versions during rollout. small config mistakes can cause duplicated state or latency spikes. 22:30 Lina (Orchid CTO): sounds reasonable. thanks all. 22:40 Maya (Redwood AE): thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the items discussed. 22:50 Recording ends.
